description.value: The study investigated the neural basis of establishing a focal point in coordination games in individuals with behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia and related coordination limitations to cortical thinning.

spans.text: In this article, we investigate the neuroanatomic basis for coordination in individuals with behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD).

value: Given the difficulties with strategic thinking and perspective taking associated with bvFTD, we predict limitations establishing a focal point in a coordination game, and expect this to be related to prefrontal disease.

spans.text: The multiple regression module in SPM5 was used to relate cortical thinning in bvFTD to the FI-difference score of each individual with bvFTD obtained from the behavioral task.

Since volumetric MRI images were only available for a subset of individuals with bvFTD (n=12), we first evaluated whether this subset exhibited the same limitations with coordination observed in the larger sample of individuals with bvFTD.

A regression analysis using the FI-difference scores revealed that coordination limitations in individuals with bvFTD were associated with cortical thinning in to DLPFC, rostral prefrontal cortex (rPFC), ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC) and anterior cingulate (see Table 1 and blue regions in Figure 2).
